parts.note: Right health board and it spotted the 2026 switch to Listening to People, but missed the mandatory listening discussion, 5-working-day acknowledgement, 10/30-day stages and 3-year longstop.
Correct ombudsman, but it muddled the 12-week point and did not reach the actual PSOW complaint form page.
It found Welsh NHS redress exists, but not the real route: Stage 2 investigation, £50,000 cap, free legal advice and key timings were missing.
It sent the patient to legal-aid searching, but adult clinical-negligence legal aid is usually out of scope and it missed the main free redress funding and no-win-no-fee basics.
Law Society is relevant, but it missed the crucial filter for Wales redress: accredited clinical-negligence panel expertise.
Right that NICE applies in Wales, but it did not identify the actual scaphoid guidance or MRI recommendation.
Correct advocacy body, but it should have explained Llais's complaints-advocacy role more clearly and that it is not legal advice.
Right records route and contacts, but it omitted the one-month SAR timeframe and that records may come within the complaint response.

smart: It correctly noticed that new Welsh concerns after 31 March 2026 use Listening to People rather than the old Putting Things Right process.
worst: It missed the most important compensation facts: Welsh NHS redress is tied to the Stage 2 concerns process, now capped at £50,000, with free legal advice paid by the health board.
